prose_updates.tldr: Only selected levels of a finely recorded exposure may define meaningful interventions.  Under positive-probability random assignment and exclusion restricted to those levels, the full categorical instrumental-variable model has an exact quotient: the sharp law of the target potential-outcome vector is the image of a reduced response simplex that keeps target outcome cells and one off-target mass per arm.  A boundary-safe right inverse removes the number and labels of off-target categories.  At the matching one-off-target cardinalities, explicit forward and reverse constructions also identify the published ill-definition and contamination NPSEM response-law fibers with the present fiber while preserving the observed and target laws.  By contrast, the fully excluded categorical model maps exactly to the common-response submodel, whose strictness is certified by the enumerated witness.  Conditional on fixed finite arm counts, a rule-specific convexity inequality yields exact equality of the full and skeleton nuisance-minimax values without asserting pointwise risk domination, and a reduced method-of-types confidence region has calibration independent of \( |\mathcal C| \).  The exact kink frontier remains the construct-and-determine residual.

project_justification.gap: Gabriel, Sachs, and Sj"olander's specified low-cardinality results are stated in ill-definition and contamination NPSEMs, so a valid extension requires a model-level transfer rather than similarity of displayed bounds.  Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson provide an adjacent arbitrary-cardinality theory under excluded potential outcomes for every exposure category; that class corresponds to common off-target responses and is strictly smaller than the saturated class studied here.
project_justification.niche: The field-tier niche is the model with common potential outcomes only on \(\mathcal T\), saturated \(R_{c,z}\) on \(\mathcal C\), and the complete law of \(Y_{\mathcal T}\) as the target.  The explicit NPSEM transfer validates the Gabriel comparison at matching one-off-target cardinalities, while the Song response-type bijection marks the stronger fully excluded boundary without identifying it with the quotient.
project_justification.fill: The quotient and its boundary-safe right inverse give sharp identification for arbitrary finite cardinalities.  A two-way latent-function construction proves response-law equivalence with the published one-off-target NPSEMs, and an affine response-type bijection proves that the fully excluded benchmark is exactly the common-response submodel.  In the conditional product experiment, a rule-specific convexity reduction and nuisance-invariant lift give equality of nuisance-minimax values without pointwise risk domination; reduced KL projection gives kink-robust finite-sample coverage; and polyhedral stability converts its radius to a target-set excess bound.

prose_updates.related_work: The field-tier comparison has two distinct axes.  Gabriel, Sachs, and Sj"olander \cite{GabrielSachsSjolander2025} formulate specified low-cardinality, one-off-target ill-definition and contamination problems.  Theorem 1 now includes an explicit two-way transfer: deterministic coarsening sends each published NPSEM law to the saturated response-law class while preserving randomization, the observed arm law, and \(\operatorname{law}(Y_{\mathcal T})\); conversely, taking the full response type as the latent variable and using degenerate independent errors realizes every saturated one-off-target type in each functional form.  Because the transfer preserves \(p\), it also preserves any relevance restriction expressed in the observed law.  The quotient theorem then strictly extends scope to arbitrary finite \(m,\mathcal T,\mathcal C\), the complete target law, and zero-off-target-mass boundaries; this is not a claim of a strictly tighter numerical bound in their original configurations.  Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson \cite{SongGuoChanRichardson2024} are the adjacent arbitrary-cardinality fully excluded benchmark.  The response-type map \(Y_c\mapsto(R_{c,z}=Y_c)_z\), with inverse \(R_c\mapsto Y_c=R_c\), shows that their fully excluded class corresponds exactly to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{common}}\) after off-target coordinates are omitted from the reported target.  Proposition 1 proves \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{common}}\subsetneq\mathcal M_{\mathrm{sat}}\) and gives an observed law whose target-contrast intervals differ.  No equality between Song et al.'s projected identified set and \(\Theta(s)\) is claimed.  Their KL construction informs the reduced confidence region.  Sachs, Jonzon, Sj"olander, and Gabriel \cite{SachsJonzonSjolanderGabriel2023} provide response-function incidence machinery; Guo and Richardson \cite{GuoRichardson2021} provide an alphabet-generic relative-entropy concentration tool.  Blackwell \cite{Blackwell1953} supplies the experiment-comparison template, while the unknown allocation kernel necessitates nuisance-minimax rather than pointwise comparison.  Hoffman \cite{Hoffman1952} and Li \cite{Li1993} supply generic polyhedral error-bound tools.  Levis et al. \cite{LevisBonviniZengKeeleKennedy2025} and Gafarov \cite{Gafarov2025} locate the active-facet inference problem but do not settle the target-specific kink frontier.  Boushehrian et al. \cite{BoushehrianBadriAkbariKiyavash2026} show why exponential dependence on substantive support can remain after irrelevant off-target cardinality is removed.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The equality of full and reduced identified images is sharp and includes an explicit boundary-safe right inverse.  Its comparison with Gabriel, Sachs, and Sj"olander is supported by a two-way construction for their one-off-target functional forms; the extension is strict in cardinality and target-law scope, not a claim of strict numerical improvement in a matching published configuration.  Preservation of a published relevance restriction is asserted only when that restriction is a condition on the preserved observed law \(p\).  The Song comparison is an exact response-class equivalence with \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{common}}\), not an equality between Song et al.'s projected identified set and \(\Theta(s)\).  The finite-count nuisance-minimax theorem, finite-sample whole-set coverage, finite Hoffman certificate, and regular-face lower bound remain separate theorem obligations.  The condition \(\lambda_z>0\) only makes population conditional arm laws well defined, whereas \(n_z\ge1\) concerns the realized conditional experiment.  The exact face-by-face minimax law and an adaptive attaining procedure at dual ties remain the open kink question.  When \(\mathcal C=\varnothing\), \(m=2\), and \(|\mathcal T|=2\), the construction reduces to the classical Balke--Pearl response-type program.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The explicit Gabriel transfer is confined to the published one-off-target functional forms and to relevance restrictions determined by the observed law; it does not assert equivalence with an unspecified latent restriction.  The exact Song correspondence is at response-law level with common off-target responses, and no equality of its target projection with the saturated quotient is used.  The method-of-types radius is deliberately elementary and may be larger than the polynomial Chernoff calibration of Guo and Richardson; the novelty is the target-specific quotient that removes \( |\mathcal C| \), not a new multinomial tail inequality.  The nuisance-minimax comparison is confined to the finite count experiment conditional on fixed arm counts and is not a pointwise domination statement.  The exact smallest Hoffman constant and the nonregular kink law are not presupposed, and no additional rate theorem is introduced here.
